title: Building on the Codex Harness — Dominik Kundel, OpenAI
talk_summary: Dominik Kundel explains the open-source Codex app server, a JSON-RPC protocol wrapping the Codex harness, and how to build custom clients on it. He highlights pinning the harness, appending developer instructions, deferred dynamic tools, per-thread config, and using app-server threads for parallel agent work.

takeaways.technique: Pin and bundle the harness version
takeaways.what_they_do: They ship the exact Codex CLI/app-server binary with the app instead of relying on the user's installed CLI, so breaking changes and missing features are controlled.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should actually ship your own version of the harness. This will eliminate so many headaches for you

takeaways.technique: Deferred dynamic tools with tool search
takeaways.what_they_do: They define extra tools but mark them deferred so they are not injected into the system prompt; the agent finds them through tool search only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: mark them as deferred loading, which means that rather than injecting them into the system prompt, it allows Codex to use a tool search tool

takeaways.technique: Append developer instructions instead of replacing base prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend appending role/client-specific developer instructions to the tuned base system prompt rather than rewriting the whole system prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we generally recommend that you actually append to that using the developer instructions

takeaways.technique: Use app-server threads for parallel agent work
takeaways.what_they_do: They use the app server's thread events and lifecycle instead of spawning many separate non-interactive exec calls when running parallel Codex threads.
The protocol lets a client set model provider, model, and sandbox network/file permissions per thread.
takeaways.evidence_quote: setting a different model provider, choosing a different model, or even doing fine-grained control on the sandbox

takeaways.technique: Generate typed bindings/schema for the pinned protocol
takeaways.what_they_do: They generate TypeScript bindings or JSON schema for the exact app-server version and bundle it with the client to control expected capabilities.
